pr_title: Avoid deadlock when processing duplicate series record
pr_body:
fixes #9169, plus another deadlock on the line before which I didn't experience but seems plausible.

`processWALSamples()` needs to be able to send on its output channel before it can read the input channel, so read to allow this in case the output channel is full.

Also update the comment describing `processWALSamples()`   - previous text seems to relate to an earlier implementation.

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ee7e0071d10e795cb78a8e50764e45cbcaf8c29a/tsdb/head_wal.go#L232

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ee7e0071d10e795cb78a8e50764e45cbcaf8c29a/tsdb/head_wal.go#L393

review_comments: We're draining `output[idx]`, but not doing anything with data and instead losing it. Is this a correct fix?
output[idx] is the slice that contains already processed samples, so it is safe to discard
Thanks for reply. If we can safely discard values from `output[idx]`, then what's its purpose? Is it used to keep two goroutines in lockstep?

`outputs[idx]` gives the slice for reuse instead of creating new slices everytime. See:
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/280eaf33f0e935c18465c7aed3dcdd7a8cdfb6c4/tsdb/head_wal.go#L280-L285
And since we will face duplicate series records not so often, the above draining won't cause any performance degradation overall.

I had the same confusion; I tried to change the comment on `processWALSamples` to explain better but maybe not enough.

As an experiment I also re-coded this buffer re-use as a `sync.Pool` and it was slower so 🤷
